name: lectern
description: 16:9 deck for research and technical talks: serif titles over a hairline rule, sans text, one vermilion accent, figure pages with labels, notes, captions and tables.

usage.when: A research talk or technical update, shown on a 16:9 screen.
usage.how: Open with title, put separator before each part, tell each result in two pages (note-wide-figure, then plot-table or profile-pictures), close with summary-table and closing. Values go in tables, paragraphs explain causes. The general layouts (title-and-content, two-content and the image grids) cover pages the result kinds do not.

fontFallback: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

default.description: Ruled rows on the page: a bold header on a pale warm band, a hairline under the header and between body rows, no outer border, no vertical rules.
A plain outline in the background's ink, 1.25 pt, no fill.

accent.description: A vermilion 2 pt outline, no fill: to point at or ring something on a figure.

card.description: A white card with a hairline border; text flows over two columns and the card grows with it.

callout.description: A pale vermilion box under a vermilion rule: a key point, a definition or a caveat.

code.description: Source code in IBM Plex Mono on a pale warm panel, highlighted; python unless the slide names another language.

title.description: Title page: the talk name large in serif above a ruled footer, the presenter at the bottom right.

usage.when: The first page of a deck.
usage.how: title holds the talk name in at most two lines; a qualifier may follow on the second line in brackets. author holds the presenter's name, right-aligned, with the affiliation or date on a second line. There is no subtitle; use title-classic for one.

separator.description: Section separator on the dark background: one section name large above the ruled footer.

usage.when: Between parts of a talk, before the first page of each part.
usage.how: title holds the section name in one or two lines. Nothing else goes on the page.

closing.description: Closing page on the dark background: one large line such as Thank you, and a contact line under the rule.

usage.when: The last page of a talk.
usage.how: title holds the closing line; contact names the presenter or an address on at most two lines.

note-figure.description: A note on the left and one labelled figure on the right.

usage.when: An abstract, or one result that needs a paragraph beside its figure.
usage.how: note holds the paragraph. label:a names the figure as (a) ...; fig:a takes a picture made at its box size or the line-plot hook. The caption is optional.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence stating the main finding

note.placeholder: The question, why it matters, what was found and what it means, in plain words.

fig:a.placeholder: Figure, drawn at its box size

caption.placeholder: One-line caption: what is shown, the marks and the conditions

note-wide-figure.description: Method page: a narrow note on the left and one wide example figure on the right.

usage.when: The first of a result's two pages: what was done, with one example such as a snapshot or a sequence.
usage.how: note says what was done; label:a and fig:a show one example; the caption names the view and the marks.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what was done

note.placeholder: What was done, how, and under which conditions.

fig:a.placeholder: Example picture, drawn at its box size

caption.placeholder: One-line caption: what is shown, the marks and the conditions

three-figures.description: Three labelled figures in a row, an optional key at the top right, and a one-line caption.

usage.when: Three parallel views or cases side by side: one object seen three ways, three conditions, three samples.
usage.how: label:a to label:c name the panels as (a) ...; fig:a to fig:c take pictures made at their box size or the line-plot hook; fig:k is an optional key for all three.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the three figures show

caption.placeholder: One-line caption: what is shown, the marks and the conditions

profile-pictures.description: A profile plot at the top left and three pictures in a row beneath it.

usage.when: One series of states: a profile along a coordinate and the pictures at the points it marks.
usage.how: fig:a is the profile, its marks pointing at exactly the states pictured in fig:b to fig:d; label:b to label:d give each picture's place on the coordinate. fig:k is the key; fig:legend is optional.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what changes along the profile

caption.placeholder: One-line caption: what is shown, the marks and the conditions

plot-table.description: A plot on the left and a table of its values on the right, with a note that follows the table down.

usage.when: The second of a result's two pages: all the data with a trend, the values in a table.
usage.how: fig:a holds the plot; table:b holds the values, one line per row; note explains a cause only, never a value, and starts below the table whatever its length.

note.placeholder: What causes the trend, in plain words.

caption.placeholder: One-line caption: what is shown, the marks and the conditions

plot-table-below.description: A short plot with a note under it on the left, and a tall table on the right.

usage.when: As plot-table when the table has many rows or four columns.
usage.how: fig:a holds the plot and note sits under it; table:b holds the values, one line per row.

note.placeholder: What causes the trend, in plain words.

caption.placeholder: One-line caption: what is shown, the marks and the conditions

plot-note.description: A plot on the left and a note on the right.

usage.when: A result whose plot needs a paragraph but no table.
usage.how: fig:a holds the plot; note explains it.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

note.placeholder: What the plot shows and why, in plain words.

caption.placeholder: One-line caption: what is shown, the marks and the conditions

summary-table.description: One full-width table with a note that follows it down.

usage.when: A summary that lists every case with its values, over as many pages as it needs.
usage.how: table:a holds every row, one line each; note follows the table and may stay empty.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the table lists

caption.placeholder: One-line caption: what is shown, the marks and the conditions

title-classic.description: A title page with a subtitle: title, a large subtitle and the presenter at the bottom left under the rule.

usage.when: A title page that needs a subtitle line.
usage.how: title in at most two lines; subtitle one phrase; author the presenter, with the affiliation or date on a second line.

section-header.description: A section name with a subtitle, on the light background.

usage.when: A section break that needs a subtitle; use separator otherwise.
usage.how: title the section name; subtitle one phrase.

agenda.description: A large title on the left and a list on the right.

usage.when: An outline of the talk.
usage.how: title one or two words; body the items, one per line.

title-only.description: Title and subtitle only; the rest of the page is free.

usage.when: A page whose content does not fit any other layout.
usage.how: title and subtitle as on every content page.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

title-and-content.description: Title, subtitle and one full-width text area.

usage.when: Text-only content.
usage.how: body holds the text.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

two-content.description: Two equal columns under the title.

usage.when: Two parallel blocks of text.
usage.how: body:a and body:b hold one text block each.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

three-content.description: Three equal columns under the title.

usage.when: Three parallel blocks of text.
usage.how: body:a to body:c hold 18 pt text.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

three-images-captions.description: Three pictures with a text block under each.

usage.when: Three items, each a picture and its explanation.
usage.how: fig:a to fig:c take pictures; body:a to body:c explain them in 18 pt.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

large-text.description: One large statement filling the page.

usage.when: A single message to stay on screen.
usage.how: title holds the statement.

title-text-content.description: Title, subtitle and text in the left column; a full-height figure on the right.

usage.when: One tall figure with text beside it.
usage.how: body holds 18 pt text; fig:a the figure.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

content-four-images.description: A text column on the left and a 2 x 2 grid of pictures.

usage.when: Four pictures that share one explanation.
usage.how: body holds 18 pt text; fig:a to fig:d fill the grid row by row.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

content-nine-images.description: A text column on the left and a 3 x 3 grid of pictures.

usage.when: Nine small pictures that share one explanation.
usage.how: body holds 18 pt text; fig:a to fig:i fill the grid row by row.

subtitle.placeholder: One sentence on what the page shows

text-and-content.description: A full-height text column and a full-height figure, with a small source line under the figure.

usage.when: Text first, figure second.
usage.how: body holds 18 pt text; fig:a the figure; source a small line under the figure.

content-and-text.description: A full-height figure and a full-height text column, with a small source line under the figure.

usage.when: Figure first, text second.
usage.how: body holds 18 pt text; fig:a the figure; source a small line under the figure.

end.description: A quiet closing page: the ruled footer of the title page and nothing else.

usage.when: A closing page with no text.
usage.how: No slots; the rule is drawn by the layout.

usage.when: Content placed by hand outside the template system.
usage.how: No slots.

guidance: A title names the page's subject; the subtitle states its finding.
The subtitle is one sentence-case sentence with no full stop.
Figures are drawn at exactly their box size; never crop or rescale a picture to fit.
